messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY:

Admission Date: [date]
Discharge Date: [date]
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient, an 82-year-old Caucasian female, was admitted to the hospital due to fatigue and a hemoglobin level of 6.2 g/dL. She had a past medical history of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, low AS, persistent hypotension, coronary artery disease, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, chronic kidney disease, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. She was noted to have evidence of heart failure exacerbation with bibasilar crackles and pedal edema. During her hospital course, she developed atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response and was transferred to the cardiac critical care unit. There was a multi-disciplinary discussion about potential treatment options, including balloon aortic valvuloplasty and subsequent TAVR. Transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) demonstrated low flow low gradient moderate to severe AS, and left heart catheterization showed areas between 1.22 and 1.42 cm2 with lower concern for severe AS. The patient was transferred back to the intermediate cardiac care unit with optimized rate control for atrial fibrillation, anticoagulation bridging, and diuresis for heart failure exacerbation. The patient also had elevated vWF activity on laboratory workup, but there was no evidence of active GI bleeding.

Discharge Medications:
The patient was discharged on oral medication regimens, which included [list of medications], to be continued as directed by a primary care physician.

Follow-up:
The patient is advised to follow up with her primary care physician, interventional cardiology services, cardiothoracic surgery, and other necessary specialists as per her routine schedule.

Discharge Condition:
The patient was discharged in stable condition with resolution of active GI bleeding, and improved heart failure exacerbation.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The admission was driven by symptomatic severe anaemia (Hb 6.2 g/dL) from gastrointestinal blood loss, likely Heyde-type bleeding given the aortic stenosis and von Willebrand workup. The discharge summary documents resolution of the GI bleeding, which makes this an unspecified gastrointestinal haemorrhage in chapter K, coded ahead of the resulting anaemia (D62) and the heart failure (I50). This is a judgement call, because no bleeding source was documented and the summary also says there was "no evidence of active GI bleeding".

CODE: K92
